justifications.c1: County aggregates only (Cambridgeshire £483k 2024-25 mixed fines, search-confirmed; Shropshire £850k over 268 sites ≈ £3.2k/site by researcher arithmetic); in-force per-day s74 maxima unconfirmed; left-behind-signs penalty can be as low as £100, and Highways News shows Anglian's £14k/£11k fines settled at £100 each.
justifications.c2: Shropshire ~45-55 charged sites per month in one county; Anglian Water 165 Norfolk overrun fines (search-confirmed), several caused by uncollected signs; frequent for a utility, but the share caused by kit left behind is unknown.
justifications.c3: Councils rely on resident reports and inspections; promoter must supply evidence to contest charges (Buckinghamshire); no quantified labour or cost of the evidence-gathering workaround.
justifications.c4: NRSWA s74 and SI 2009/303 overrun charging, 2026 extension to weekends (HAUC), Red Book statutory code, burden of proof on promoter, plus enforcement totals from Cambridgeshire, Shropshire and Norfolk; rule penalises overruns rather than mandating records.
justifications.c5: Street Works Manager adverts (Carrington West, Matchtech) evidence the role responsible for NRSWA compliance; who holds the s74 budget (utility vs TM contractor) is not shown, and large utilities imply enterprise procurement.
justifications.c6: TM contractors (Streetwise UK) deliver and collect kit for utilities; HRS sells monitored signs and DepotNet sells s74-risk software, but no evidence the site-visiting TM contractors resell tracking.
justifications.c7: HRS Intelliframe (UK, search-confirmed) already offers GPS sign frames with overrun alerts and portal integration, plus US Site 20/20 and Zonar; no prices anywhere and the gap (barrier-foot form factor/price) is asserted.
justifications.c8: Concept proven by deployed GPS sign frames (Intelliframe, ≥1-year battery per datasheet) and barrier impact trackers; no BOM, battery or certification evidence searched; rugged roadside environment.
justifications.c9: Every permit creates a new evidence need and charging was extended in 2026, but no comparable subscription price was found.
justifications.c10: Council enforcement releases (Cambridgeshire, Gloucestershire), local press (Great Yarmouth Mercury, Brighton & Hove News, Shropshire Star), trade press (Highways News) and first-hand complaints (Alton Herald letter, FixMyStreet report).

weakest: The money per left-behind-kit incident is small or negotiated down (£100 penalties; £14k fines settled at £100), and HRS Intelliframe already sells GPS sign monitoring with overrun alerts in the UK.
